column1: # Swarm repository test audit ledger v1
# This is the single committed authority for deciding which tracked tests and
# test-like programs Swarm should keep, change, delete, repair, quarantine, or
# re-tier. It is an audit ledger, not an instruction to edit product/test code.
# Inventory totals: 5568 review rows across 953 tracked files.
# UTF-8 tab-separated values. Lines beginning with # are policy; the first
# uncommented line is the header. Fields must remain single-line; use concise
# semicolon-separated evidence. Do not add tabs or newlines inside values.
# test_id is stable for kind/path/symbol. source_sha256 fingerprints the entire
# source file at inventory time. line is navigation help only, not identity. The
# final schema_version field is immutable and prevents empty-field TSV line endings.
# 1. Integrate this pristine ledger commit before launching any review wave.
# 2. Assign exactly one pass1_batch per first-pass coder. A coder may edit only
#    and pass1_validation on rows in that batch. They must read every assigned
#    source file and every listed definition/callsite; files are never split.
# 3. Integrate all pass-one batches before starting pass two. Regenerate no rows
#    and do not change test_id/source_sha256/batch columns mid-audit.
# 4. Pass-two batches intentionally preserve pass-one file boundaries to make
#    one-file integration safe. Assign each to a coder who reviewed none of its
#    source files in pass one. That coder independently rereads the source and
#    current contract before inspecting pass one, then edits only pass2_reviewer,
# 5. Ledger-writing Coder batches share one owned path and therefore must launch,
#    complete, and integrate sequentially; never put two ledger writers in one
#    concurrent wave. Parallel read-only research may return evidence to the one
#    current ledger owner but must not modify this file. On integration, retain
#    reviewed rows and apply only the incoming owned batch; never use a whole-file
# 6. Reviewers do not modify tests or production code during either audit pass.
#    Remediation begins only from agreed final rows in separate scoped changes.
# 7. Before reviewing a row, compare source_sha256 with the current file. If it
#    differs, use needs-reinventory and explain the drift; never classify changed
# First pass states the behavior/assertion, why it is current or retired, and
# exact authority (implementation symbol, checked-in contract/doc, replacement
# test, or observed focused result). Passing is not proof of value; failing is
# not proof of obsolescence. Do not restore retired APIs or weaken fail-closed
# behavior to satisfy a test. Validation records an exact bounded command/result
# or not-run plus why. Tests are not run merely to fill this file.
# The auditor independently determines a verdict before relying on pass-one
# rationale. agree confirms both disposition and evidence. disagree records the
# auditor's proposed first-pass verdict and exact contrary evidence. For agree,
# set final_status=agreed and resolution to the confirmed pass-one verdict. For
# disagree, set final_status=disputed and leave resolution blank. Missing runtime
# evidence maps to blocked-evidence; source drift maps to stale-inventory. Disputes
# get no remediation action until a later owner decision. pass1_reviewer and
# pass2_reviewer must be different durable session/agent identifiers.
# Go nested rows represent static t.Run/b.Run callsites; reviewers inspect all
# table-driven cases reachable from the containing definition even when case
# count/names are dynamic. File-review rows cover structured test files without
# static top-level definitions. standalone-candidate covers every tracked .sh and
# .mjs program, including utilities, so its actual role receives an explicit
# decision. Benchmarks/nested calls are additional to the 5,168 headline tests.
